title: Oscar and the Spire
premise: Paloma Underhill, a mercenary bound by a dead god's covenant, has spent years hiding among the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, trading in relics and rumors while pretending his oath died with his deity. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin receiving answers—twisted, hungry ones—Paloma learns his silent god was not dead but imprisoned in the Spire at the world's edge, and that the guild's founder engineered the silence to seize divine power. Torn between loyalty to the guild that sheltered him and the truth of what it did, Paloma gathers the scattered fragments of the broken covenant and climbs the Spire as the long winter falls. In the climax he must choose: restore his god and lose his own name and memories as payment, or let the covenant die. He reforges it with a third option—binding himself into the covenant as a mortal witness—ending the winter, freeing a diminished but honest god, and leaving him neither mercenary nor servant, but something new.
about_author: Ines Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging medieval oaths and contracts before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people trapped by promises they no longer believe in.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. In the guildhouse of impossible things, Paloma appraises a relic that hums with a prayer someone answered—a thing that should be impossible since the gods went silent. His old training stirs; his scarred oath-mark aches for the first time in nine years. Emotional beat: uneasy normalcy cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Answers Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Across the city, answered prayers turn predatory—a child's wish for snow brings killing frost; a widow's plea returns her husband wrong. The guild quietly buys up every answered-prayer relic. Paloma realizes the answers share one voice, and it is not his god's. Emotional beat: dread replacing curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Founder Kept
chapters.summary: POV Paloma, with an interlude from guild-founder Vess's sealed memoirs. Digging in the restricted archive, Paloma finds proof: Vess orchestrated the gods' silence, imprisoning them in the Spire to monopolize divinity. His own god's silence was collateral, not death. Emotional beat: betrayal—the guild that saved him built the cage.

chapters.title: The Oath That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. His covenant mark flares fully awake; fragments of his god's voice reach him through dream-ledgers, asking not for worship but for witness. Guild enforcers suspect his research. His oldest friend, Sable, covers for him—and asks questions he can't answer. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling two directions.

chapters.title: A Market of Broken Things
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sent to buy back a dangerous relic, Sable discovers Paloma's secret dealings and confronts him. He tells her the truth about Vess; she chooses the guild over him—or seems to—and reports only half of what she learned. Emotional beat: heartbreak disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Vess, aware of the leak, accelerates her ritual: the false god she's grown from stolen prayers needs the last covenant fragment—carried unknowingly by Paloma—to finish falling into winter and full dominion. The city freezes; the guild turns on its own ledger-keeper. Emotional beat: hunted, exposed, out of time.

chapters.title: Fragments and Forgiveness
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Fleeing north with Sable, who defected after seeing the frozen city, Paloma recovers the scattered covenant pieces from shrines his god's faithful once kept. Each fragment costs a memory of his old life. Sable carries what he forgets. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness intertwined.

chapters.title: The Spire at the Edge of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. They climb the frozen Spire through trials made of unanswered prayers—every plea his god ever ignored stands embodied on the stairs. Paloma must face each one honestly, neither excusing nor despairing. Sable nearly turns back; he gives her his last warm memory to carry down. Emotional beat: reckoning without flinching.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. At the summit, Vess offers him partnership: keep his name, his memories, his survival—just hand over the fragment. Instead Paloma shatters her false god and reforges the covenant with a new term: a mortal witness bound within it, so gods can never again go unheard. Vess falls with her creation. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into authorship.

chapters.title: Ledger of a Living Covenant
chapters.summary: POV Sable, then Paloma. Winter breaks. Paloma descends changed—diminished, missing years, but free, his god now small, honest, and present. He reopens the guild under new terms, trading in possible things, with Sable as his partner and keeper of what he lost. Emotional beat: quiet hope; identity rebuilt rather than restored.
